items.title: Dave Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, Connecticut, November 21, 2001
items.q: the center of that piece is Martin Luther King saying we must live together as brothers or die together as fools.

ctx.x: But whether or not people want to hear something is not usually your goal about writing is it? I mean your thinking—

I’ll do that, and maybe I won’t send it to anybody it’ll just be around the house. Or maybe there’ll come a time when I think it’s right to do this. I had written one piece, a setting of Robert Penn Warren. And there came a time when it was right to do that, and it was for the soldiers that had fought in the Korean War. It ends up, the last sentence is “truth is for the grave.” Now that’s a pretty sad thing. I said to my wife, “remember that piece? Remember how it worked? We did it with the veterans in New York?”…
In this current situation we’re in now, with different philosophies and different religions involved, can you see a way to best resolve what’s going on?
